editorial.headline: Industrial Design, Nationally Open but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 74119 spans industrial design for a broad range of products, open nationally to full foreign ownership yet unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 74119 covers industrial design activity for products across a broad range of practical uses. Its scope includes design for timekeeping, measuring and office equipment; brushing products; tools and hardware; photographic, cinematographic and optical equipment; musical equipment; office stationery; sales and advertising equipment; and hunting and fishing equipment. It also reaches products for fluid distribution, ventilation, air-conditioning and heating, solid fuels, lighting, construction elements, firefighting, animal care, food, tobacco and cigarettes, and crafts. The record expressly includes this design activity when it is carried out through specialist software.

For businesses, the record admits this activity at the Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales. That gives the category a wide organisational reach, from smaller design operations to large enterprises, while keeping the subject of registration clear: industrial design for the listed product fields. The range is functional: it moves from office and measuring equipment to climate-control, lighting, construction, firefighting, food, tobacco and craft products. A timekeeping device, an optical tool, a lighting product or a firefighting product may sit far apart in the market, but each illustrates the same through-line in this record: the design of an industrial product.

For PMA at the national level, the position is just as clear. The activity is marked open, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%, referenced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. A foreign investor therefore encounters no national foreign-ownership cap below full ownership in the supplied record. That national reading matters, but it is not the final answer for a Bali registration.

Bali’s position is different and decisive. A foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. The record marks it blocked by risk class because OSS risk at the Large scale is Low or Medium-Low on every scope; Bali’s moratorium of May 2026 blocks PMA registration for all KBLI carrying those risk levels. The provincial rule is island-wide and permanent. National openness does not override Bali’s island-wide, permanent PMA block for the risk classes recorded here. This is not a Bali-specific reduction of the 100% national ceiling. It is a territorial bar on PMA registration in Bali, even though the activity remains nationally open.
